name: Lume
description: `lume upgrade` does Deno import() of remote TypeScript from a CDN — downloads+executes, no sig/checksum.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Lume's `upgrade` CLI command delegates to the imported upgrade implementation for the current project and awaits it. The reviewed command file does not itself establish the remote CDN, module execution, or signature/checksum behavior of that delegated implementation.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than historical release re-verification; the imported upgrade implementation, CDN transport, and any signature/checksum behavior were not independently connected to this command body.

original_evidence.text: | Lume | lumeland/lume | Deno static site generator (CLI) | Y | N (explicit `lume upgrade` command only) | Y | https (`fetch()`/dynamic `import()` over HTTPS to jsdelivr, standard TLS only — no extra validation) | N — no signed manifest of any kind | none (no hash pinning, no signature check, no checksum comparison; relies solely on HTTPS/TLS transport to the CDN) | N/A (no verifying key exists) | `cli/upgrade.ts:1-6` imports `upgrade` from `../deps/init.ts` and calls it when the user runs `lume upgrade` (registered as a CLI subcommand in `cli.ts:4-18,109`). `deps/init.ts:1-11`: `fetch("https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/package/gh/lumeland/init")` retrieves the version list, picks `data.versions.shift()` (i.e., trusts the first entry returned by the CDN's JSON API with no signature/hash check), then does `await import(\`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lumeland/init@${version}/mod.ts\`)` and `await import(\`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lumeland/init@${version}/upgrade.ts\`)` — Deno's dynamic `import()` of a remote URL both downloads and executes that TypeScript/JS module directly, with only HTTPS/TLS as the integrity mechanism (no code signing, no checksum manifest). This is a real download-and-execute path, but it only fires on the explicit, user-invoked `lume upgrade` command — not automatically on every run. |
